answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a slow trust bridge: a new identity starts with almost no rights and must build a verifiable record of useful work over many epochs before it can vote or earn. Like crossing a canyon, there is no shortcut — an attacker must pay the full time and compute cost for every fake identity, while a reef of established peers only trusts identities whose history they can inspect. Cloning identities therefore costs as much as building real ones, so farming them stops paying.
